title: the MotP Negative Quasi-Planes
audit_comment: the Negative Quasi-Planes, printed pp. 57-59, the four in one round: Vacuum, Ash, Dust and Salt - the increasing-absence doctrine (what is missing in the Positive is present here, thinning toward the Negative), the per-plane survival (the Vacuum hold-breath-only rule with the airy-element uselessness, the 1-HD-per-round elemental loss and the 1,000-yard doubled infravision; the Ash warmth depletion with the fire-creature drain and the cold-protection halving at 30 yards; the Dust crumbling with the gaseous-form protection and the 10d3 vision; the Salt per-TURN elemental drain), the tenuous movement (falling fastest, the borders discourage it), the 1-in-10-per-12-hours encounter check AMENDED against the report's 1-in-20 (the 1-20/21-00 phenomenon/creature split, no elemental pockets), the black wall intrusion at 3d6 per round for 2d10 turns, the 1-in-10 native life-level drain per touch, the native rules (the Ash flee-or-explode save vs. poison at 1d4 per hit die within 20 feet, the Dust 50% split with the earth-spell immunity, the Salt water-shatter with the 30-foot shard radius), the magic decay (the Vacuum same-round dissipation, the 1d4-round Dust and Salt rules), the doubled guide prices, no archoments, and the Foreword doctrines riding this round (the Fibber McGee closet, what-has-been-written-is-true, the made-it-up admission).

banner.title: THE MotP NEGATIVE QUASI-PLANES - printed pp. 57-59, the four in one round: Vacuum, Ash, Dust and Salt - the increasing-absence doctrine, the per-plane survival ladder, the black wall, the level-drain natives, and the Foreword doctrines riding the round that closes the inner half.
banner.provenance: verified against printed pp. 57-59 of the uploaded motp.pdf OCR (and p. 3 for the Foreword); the quasi-planes pin by mapping onto the major-plane frame (Vacuum as Air, Ash as Fire, Dust as Earth, Salt as Water) with the MotP's own absence dangers carried explicitly; the encounter frequency AMENDED against the source (1 in 10 per 12 hours, not the report's 1-in-20).
banner.sentinel: the gap census after this round: 42 closed, 48 open - three boxes fall (the quasi-group, the encounter frequency, the Foreword); the inner half of the book closes here, and the Astral chapter (pp. 60-72) opens the second half next.

consts.name: dddQuasiPlaneCount
consts.comment: the four negative quasi-planes between the Negative Material and the majors: Vacuum (Air), Ash (Fire), Dust (Earth), Salt (Water) - the increasing-absence doctrine: what is missing in the Positive is present here, thinning toward the Negative itself.

consts.name: dddVacuumHdLossPerRound
consts.comment: the Vacuum survival: no breathable element exists there, airy element and the like are useless, only holding one's breath sustains life; elementals and airy creatures lose 1 HD per round.

consts.name: dddVacuumVisionYards
consts.comment: the Vacuum vision: 1,000 yards, or double the normal infravision range - the plane is dark and empty but transparent.

consts.name: dddAshVisionYards
consts.comment: the Ash survival: warmth depletion, a bone-chilling cold; fire creatures lose 1 HD or level per round, warm creatures take 2d6 per round halved by cold protection; vision 30 yards.

consts.name: dddQuasiVisionDieSides
consts.comment: the Dust and Salt vision: 10d3 yards of grey half-light - the Dust blackness of crumbling matter, the Salt haze of the brine residue.

consts.name: dddDepletionDamageDieSides
consts.comment: the 2d6-per-round depletion: Ash warmth-loss in warm creatures (halved by cold protection), Dust crumbling in solids (death at 0 hp; gaseous form protects; Earth, Ooze and Magma elementals lose 1 HD per round), Salt dehydration in non-water creatures.

consts.name: dddSaltElementalTurnLoss
consts.comment: the Salt rule: water elementals - including Ice, Steam and Ooze but NOT Magma - lose 1 HD or level per TURN (not per round); salt is the residue of evaporation, and the natives thirst for water.

consts.name: dddBlackWallAdvanceDieSides
consts.comment: the Negative intrusion: a black wall of pure Negative Material advancing 3d6 inches per round for 2d10 turns; a traveler caught within loses sight of the border after 1d4 rounds - full Negative immersion effects.

consts.name: dddEncounterDenom
consts.comment: the encounter check: 1 in 10 per 12 hours (AMENDED against the source - the gap report said 1-in-20, the printed text says 1 in 10); roll 1-20 Negative Energy Phenomenon, 21-00 creature; there are NO elemental pockets in the negative quasi-planes.

bools.name: dddNativeLevelDrain
bools.comment: 1 in 10 creatures encountered are natives of the quasi-plane, and every native drains one life level per touch regardless of form.

bools.name: dddAshNativeRule
bools.comment: the Ash natives: cold grey forms; bring anything warm (even room-temperature) within 20 feet and each must save vs. poison - flee the area or explode for 1d4 per hit die; their touch drains 1d6 of body heat; invisible-force Vacuum natives hibernate in pockets of air.

bools.name: dddDustNativeRule
bools.comment: the Dust natives: 50% chance to split into two smaller forms when struck, immune to earth-affecting spells, pass through their plane's matter; stepping into their dust inflicts 2d6 per round.

bools.name: dddSaltNativeRule
bools.comment: the Salt natives: water shatters them into shards; they attack in a 30-foot radius at their hit-die level, each shard dealing 1d4 damage.

bools.name: dddMagicDecayRule
bools.comment: the magic decay: Vacuum dissipates cloud-type magic the same round it is cast; Ash extinguishes long-term flames in 1 round; Dust crumbles objects in 1d4 rounds; Salt absorbs watery magic and free water in 1d4 rounds.

bools.name: dddGuidePriceDoubled
bools.comment: the negative quasi-features: slow, plodding natives; guides always cost at least double (mists and perfumes for Steam's cousins, burned valuables for Ash, ground powders for Dust; Vacuum guides unknown); no archoments rule these planes; the elemental-roped citadels reach here from the tower ring.

bools.name: dddForewordDoctrine
bools.comment: the Foreword (p. 3) riding this round: the Fibber McGee closet frame - the planes as the stuff crammed into a closet; what-has-been-written-is-true is the ruling doctrine; the sense-of-wonder caveat; and the made-it-up admission (Jeff Grubb).
